chunks: Ibn Abi Jayyid al-Qummi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from Abdullah ibn al-Abbas ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from Abu al-Fadl al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said:
I came to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them) at Samarrah, and I congratulated him on the birth of his son (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad (title of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari)
key_terms.سَمَرَّاءَ: Samarrah (city in Iraq where the Imams resided)

ai.seo_question: Who congratulated Imam al-Askari on the birth of his son?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides a foundational historical account of the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (aj) during the Minor Ghaiba, specifically noting the narrator's visit to Imam al-Hasan al-Askari in Samarrah. It serves as a primary evidence for the lineage and timing of the Twelfth Imam, reinforcing the Shia belief in his physical existence prior to his occultation. The narration highlights the continuity of the Imamate through the progeny of Imam al-Husayn, linking the event to the broader eschatological narrative of salvation.
